observations: Selected 0.6 kWh for 100 W running a quarter of a 24-hour day.
Tests gave 0.6 versus 2.4 kWh. Minimum one hour gave 0.025 versus 0.1 kWh.
Screenshot showed both lines almost on the baseline against 4.8 kWh full scale at one hour. Reveal preserved original/current values and explained active-time fraction and constant on-power.
whyCool: A power label does not tell you daily energy without active time.
caveat: Assumes constant 25% duty and zero off-power; fixed graph scale makes small intervals visually subtle.
effort: Prediction, both tests, minimum duration, screenshot and reveal.

prediction.reason: Specific plausible always-on misconception with sufficient inputs.

interaction.reason: Duration change scales both assumptions consistently.

payoff.reason: Explains why rated power alone is insufficient.
payoff.evidence: Multiply elapsed time by on-time fraction.

transfer.reason: Appliance variability and duration assumptions constrain applying model.
transfer.evidence: Check own ratings and tariffs; toy model.

visualExplanation.reason: Common-scale lines support comparison but short-interval detail is hard to see.

depth.reason: Separates power, elapsed duration and duty fraction.
